final_answer: Lowering corporate tax rates doesn't reliably boost long-term job growth because the primary benefit typically goes to shareholders via buybacks and dividends rather than worker wages or new hiring. Empirical studies of multiple US state tax cuts found no statistically significant gain in employment. When corporations save on taxes, they often prioritize capital allocation toward financial engineering over expanding their workforce—especially when economic demand remains weak and automation continues replacing middle-skill roles. Long-term job growth depends more fundamentally on factors like education quality, infrastructure, immigration policy, healthcare access, and general business confidence than on corporate tax rates alone. At the federal level in particular, a single rate cut affects all states uniformly, providing no competitive advantage for any specific employer to hire more workers.
